programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Programme exploring the cultural significance of the banana. The Velvet Underground's John Cale tells the story behind Andy Warhol's famous LP cover, Auberon Waugh and John Walters recall their first encounters with the fruit after the war, and footballer Brendan Batson considers how they became a symbol of racism hurled from the terraces.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Masterpieces
programme.desc: Bendor Grosvenor and Emma Dabiri travel to the grand Georgian mansion of Tatton Park in Cheshire, where Bendor has spotted a mysterious portrait of a 16th-century physician in its collection.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Valerie Pitts, David Attenborough and Tony Lewis. Featuring guest musician Steuart Bedford.

programme.title: Earth's Natural Wonders
programme.desc: A look at some of the most extreme places on the planet, including Mount Everest and the Grand Canyon, and the challenges facing their inhabitants.

programme.title: Great Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Palin travels through Northern Ireland and Ireland and finds out more about his Irish ancestors, experiences the peace train from Belfast to Dublin, and visits Cork.

programme.title: Michael Palin: The Art of Travel
programme.desc: Michael Palin takes his golf clubs to St Andrews on a journey up the `drier side of Britain', where the London North Eastern Railway's publicity department of the 1920s and 1930s promoted an industrial service alongside more familiar holiday resorts.

programme.title: Comic Roots
programme.desc: An enjoyable look at Michael Palin's formative years, as he talks about his early interest in acting and comedy, taking in Shrewsbury School and Oxford.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: A look at the violent five-day standoff between inmates and law enforcement which gripped America in 1971.

programme.title: Dan Cruickshank and the Family That Built Gothic Britain
programme.desc: As good as any Dickens novel, this is the triumphant and tragic story of the greatest architectural dynasty of the 19th century. Dan Cruickshank charts the rise of Sir George Gilbert Scott to the very heights of success, the fall of his son George Junior and the rise again of his grandson Giles It is a story of architects bent on a mission to rebuild Britain. From the romantic heights of the Midland Hotel at St Pancras station to the modern image of Bankside power station.

programme.title: Tornado: The 100mph Steam Engine
programme.desc: The new A1 class steam engine Tornado tries to achieve 100mph on the main line. The secret speed attempt will be made in the dead of night. If it tops the ton it will be the first time in 50 years steam has gone this fast.

programme.title: The Return of the Flying Scotsman
programme.desc: Following the Flying Scotsman, the world's most famous steam engine, as it returns to the tracks following a ten-year restoration which cost more than £4 million. We are on board the train for its final test runs on the East Lancashire Railway.

programme.title: Flying Scotsman: Sounds from the Footplate
programme.desc: Enjoy the view from the driving seat of the world's most famous steam locomotive as Flying Scotsman travels the length of the Severn Valley Railway, with `cab cameras' capturing all the action from the footplate.

programme.title: Ian Hislop Goes off the Rails
programme.desc: Ian Hislop takes a look at the notorious Beeching Report of 1963, which led to the closure of a third of the nation's railway lines and stations and forced tens of thousands of people into the car and onto the road. He investigates the fallout from the plan, discovering what was lost to the British landscape, communities and ways of life when the railway map shrank.

programme.title: Waris Hussein Remembers... The Clothes in the Wardrobe
programme.desc: Director Waris Hussein talks about his memories of making the 1993 TV drama `The Clothes in the Wardrobe', adapted from the Alice Thomas Ellis novel by Martin Sherman. Waris talks about the power of choice that the story represents.

programme.title: Screen Two
programme.desc: England 1950s. Nineteen-year-old Margaret is unhappily about to marry a dull middle-aged man. As the wedding draws closer, the guests arrive, including the free-spirited Lili, who forms an unholy alliance with the groom's mother, determined to ruin the wedding. Drama based on the Summerhouse Trilogy novels by Alice Thomas Ellis.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: A look at the taboo that is corporal punishment. Today it is a subject that is almost impossible to discuss in public, but it's not that long since corporal punishment was a routine part of life.

programme.title: The Railway Children
programme.desc: Based on Edith Nesbit's book about three children whose lives change dramatically after they move from a comfortable townhouse to a small Yorkshire cottage near a railway line. Their mother is forced to make the move after their father was wrongly imprisoned, but the children, ignorant of the circumstances, soon settle into their new home, enchanted by the countryside and enthralled by the railway.

programme.title: Big Screen Britain
programme.desc: Ben Fogle visits classic film locations. He and Sally Thomsett, who played Phyllis in the 1972 film of The Railway Children, wander the streets of Haworth and visit the Bronte Parsonage, which served as the doctor's house.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: The Trains That Time Forgot: Britain's Lost Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Timeshift journeys back to a lost era of rail travel, when trains had names, character and style. Once the pride of the railway companies that ran them, the named train is now largely consigned to railway history. Writer and presenter Andrew Martin asks why we once named trains and why we don't do so anymore. He embarks on three railway journeys around Britain, following the routes of three of the most famous named trains - the Flying Scotsman, the Cornish Riviera Express and the Brighton Belle.

programme.title: Carrie
programme.desc: Carrie White is a shy young girl who doesn't make friends easily. After her classmates taunt her about her horrified reaction to her totally unexpected first period, one of them takes pity on her and gets Tommy Ross, her boyfriend and class hunk to invite Carrie to the senior prom. Meanwhile, another girl who has been banned from the prom for her continued aggressive behaviour is not as forgiving. Based on the book by Stephen King.

programme.title: The Elephant Man
programme.desc: Based on the life of John Merrick, a man born with a disfiguring disease who seemed doomed to a grim existence as a sideshow freak until taken in by a London surgeon and introduced to society. Despite his dreadful experiences, Merrick is a gentle, intelligent soul and becomes a popular guest in Victorian drawing rooms - but only if his deformed features are completely covered.
